title: What opening gives the half circle, and how long is AX?
description: The wave along a line AB of eight centimetres is solved for the two numbers the book asks for. The video halves AB to get AX, then halves AX to get the opening of the compass, and checks both against the line.
teaching_notes: One idea: the opening of the compass is half of the flat side of the half circle, and the flat side is half of the central line. Watch for children who give four centimetres for the opening.

source: What radius should be taken in the compass to get this half circle? What should be the length of AX?
video_script.why: The child finds AX and the opening of the compass by the same halving method as the solved wave.
video_script.substitution: The line AB of eight centimetres with X halfway.
video_script.anchor: The wave along the central line AB of the book
video_script.payoff_line: The radius is two centimetres and eigh X is four centimetres.

final_answer.spoken: the radius is two centimetres and eigh X is four centimetres

never_show: the answer before the last beat
maths_rules: AB = 8 cm and X is halfway: AX = 8 / 2 = 4 cm.
Check: a half circle of radius 2 cm is 2 + 2 = 4 cm wide, equal to AX.
video_script.design: One idea: halve AB, then halve AX. Uses the method of the solved wave. The line AB stays all video.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>What opening should the compass have to draw it, and how long is eigh X?

<bookmark mark='tip'/>The compass tip sits in the middle of that side.
<bookmark mark='open'/>The opening reaches from the tip to the curve, and that is the radius.

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the line eigh B is eight centimetres, with two equal half circles on it.

beats.on_screen: To find: a) the radius for the compass; b) the length of AX

marks.find: the line To find is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the radius for the compass, and the length of eigh X.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the two waves share AB equally, so AX = 8 / 2 = 4 cm

marks.share: X is marked halfway on the line

narration: <bookmark mark='share'/>Step one, work the same way as the example in your book.
The two waves share the line equally.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Eight divided by two gives four, so eigh X is four centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: radius = half of AX = 4 / 2 = 2 cm

marks.half: AX is halved at the tip position

narration: <bookmark mark='half'/>Step two, the tip goes in the middle of eigh X.
The radius is half of eigh X.
<bookmark mark='rad'/>Four divided by two gives two centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 3 (check): the width 2 + 2 = 4 cm equals AX; AX + XB = 4 + 4 = 8 cm equals AB

marks.wide: the half circle is measured across and reads two plus two
marks.whole: the two halves of the line are added to give the whole line

narration: <bookmark mark='wide'/>Step three, check the answers.
A half circle with this radius is two plus two wide.
That is four centimetres, the same as eigh X.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>Two such waves give four plus four, which is eight centimetres.
That is the same as eigh B.

beats.on_screen: Answer: a) radius 2 cm; b) AX = 4 cm
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The radius is two centimetres and eigh X is four centimetres.
